bullets.title: MU: Massive F4Q/F1Q beat; supply tight through CY28, buybacks starting Dec
bullets.body: Micron F4Q revenue $54.23B (+5.7% vs consensus) and EPS $33.42 (+$1.70); F1Q guided $61.5B revenue (+7.1% above Street) and $38.15 EPS (+7.6%). Management called supply-demand "tighter in CY27 and CY28 than CY26," with >75% of 2027 output committed via 26 strategic customer agreements covering ~35% of revenue through CY30. HBM pricing for CY27 "materially above" CY26. F1Q gross margin guided at 86.25% (floor for FY27, improving thereafter). Buybacks resume Dec 9 with 100%+ excess FCF return. Sell-side 95% buy; PTs range $1200 (MS) to $2000 (Susquehanna); Wolfe raises FY27 EPS to $174, PT $1,500; UBS $1,625; Citi raises PT to $1,300; Mizuho raises to $1,400. Stock -0.7% pre-mkt on mixed gross margin trajectory despite strong guide.

bullets.title: ACN: Biggest beat in ~5 years; +17% pre-mkt on bookings inflection and FY27 guide
bullets.body: Accenture F4Q revenue $18.68B vs $18.04B consensus (+7% CC, well above 1-5% guidance); EPS $3.29 vs $3.19. Bookings $22.2-22.7B accelerated from -3% to +5% y/y. FY27 CC revenue growth guided +3-6% (above Street +1-3.9%); FY27 EPS $14.39-$14.81 vs $14.64 consensus. Quarterly dividend raised 4.9% to $1.71. UBS upgraded to Buy; Mizuho Outperform ($226 PT). AI disintermediation fears easing as AI work converts to durable revenue. All regions grew ~7% CC with EMEA and Americas accelerating materially.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Gemini 4 Argon removes key overhang; Citi reiterates Buy $447, JPM raises PT to $420
bullets.body: Google launched Gemini 4 Argon, ranking top across 14 of 19 benchmarks vs GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1/Opus 5.5, with 1M-token output limit (vs prior 64K) and aggressive pricing at $2/$10 per 1M input/output tokens (95% cached discount). Citi reiterates Buy $447, calling it a "restart of Google's product cycle"; JPM raises Dec-27 PT to $420, reiterating OW. Caveats: internal employee skepticism on real-world coding performance vs benchmarks; currently limited to cyber defenders and US government with broader rollout pending. Stock was -15% from May highs ahead of launch; GOOGL +1.4% pre-mkt.

bullets.title: AVGO: Lends Anthropic $42B for infrastructure; expands Google TPU deal through 2031
bullets.body: Broadcom agreed to lend Anthropic up to $42B (convertible to common stock) to finance infrastructure purchases, covering roughly one-third of Anthropic's $125B five-year TPU commitment. Separately, Broadcom extended its long-term agreement to supply custom TPUs to Google through 2031 and expanded strategic collaboration with Google and Anthropic for ~3.5 gigawatts of AI compute capacity starting 2027.

bullets.title: CRDO: Jefferies BUY $270; OmniConnect/Positron AI deal seen as $1B+ rev driver in 2H27
bullets.body: Jefferies reiterates Buy on CRDO at $270 PT after NDR. OmniConnect ramping with Positron AI (raised $875M at $5B valuation, planning hundreds-of-MW Titan Rack deployments) offers $2-3k content per XPU and potential $1B+ revenue. Blackwell deployment implies 50-100% upside to current AEC guidance ($130-150M/qtr). CRDO to demonstrate first MicroLED-powered ALC and introduce MicroVCSEL roadmap at OCP in October. Stock +2.1% pre-mkt.

bullets.title: MSFT: JPM reiterates OW $625; Cloud ROIC stabilizing at 32-33% despite capex intensity
bullets.body: JPM notes Microsoft's resegmented A&I segment generates $268B revenue at 50%+ operating margins and ~80% of total OI. Cloud ROIC estimated at ~37% in FY26, expected to stabilize at 32-33% FY27E-FY31E — second among hyperscalers behind Google (38%). High-margin software stack (M365, GitHub, Security) layered on shared GPU/CPU infrastructure is key differentiator. Hedgeye signals MSFT bullish range 496-525.

bullets.title: META: Muse surpasses 3M weekly users in <1 month; Morgan Stanley $775 PT, OW
bullets.body: Meta Muse reached 3M weekly active users within 23 days of launch, driving AMD EPYC CPU orders into 2028. Morgan Stanley values the cost-to-serve model as a competitive moat, estimating CPU capacity acquired in CY26 to serve 1B Muse DAUs is already embedded in $209B FY27 opex model; maintains OW with $775 PT at 21x NTM. JPM notes META has gained versus GOOGL narrative as Meta builds strong products without needing frontier models. Hedgeye signals META bullish range 678-790.

bullets.title: ORCL: +1.86% pre-mkt on $7B Tencent AI chip lease; Project Jupiter air permit on track
bullets.body: Tencent signed a ~$7B five-year lease with Oracle for 100k advanced AI chips across Southeast Asia data centers (~30% upfront). Separately, Project Jupiter (ORCL/BE data center) NM air permit delay expected to push the Nov 23 deadline to mid-December due to hearing-officer vacancy — experts view as timing risk not approval risk; post-permit EIB appeal timeline 4-8 months. Delays appear adequately priced into ORCL shares; timely approval should alleviate RPO-to-revenue conversion concerns.

bullets.title: CRWV: Multiple bullish notes; 10% price increase signals pricing power; OPCO Outperform $150
bullets.body: OPCO reiterates Outperform $150 on CoreWeave, noting Vera Rubin NVL72 deployment reinforces fastest hardware-to-capacity advantage and the company is transitioning from training to production AI. CRWV announced a 10% price increase at Fully Connected conference; Piper reiterates top pick, citing Forge software unifying pre/post training and inference. AI data center regulatory headwinds (permitting, moratoriums) benefit capacity holders with approved sites like CRWV.

bullets.title: AMZN: Goldman adds to Conviction List; cited for AI/AWS/advertising momentum
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs added Amazon to its October US Conviction List, citing accelerating AI, AWS, advertising, and eCommerce profitability trends. Separately, AMZN agreed to buy 690 MW from Constellation Energy supporting Maryland nuclear expansion. Hedgeye signals AMZN bearish range 240-255, flagging divergence with GS conviction thesis.

bullets.title: HPE: Citi raises PT to $92; FY27 networking guided high-teens to low-20%, Vultr $1.2B order
bullets.body: HPE boosted FY27 networking revenue growth guidance to high-teens to low-20%; increased Juniper synergies to $800M annually by FY28 (from $600M) and outlined high-teens networking CAGR through FY29 with ~50%+ AI data center networking growth. Vultr announced a $1.2B AMD Helios AI Rack order validating HPE's AI systems strategy. Citi raises PT to $92 (from $76), maintaining Buy. Morgan Stanley maintains OW with $72 PT.

bullets.title: MDB: Wolfe removes from Alpha List on CEO turnover; D.A. Davidson Buy on field feedback
bullets.body: Wolfe Research removed MongoDB from its Alpha List, citing CEO turnover creating uncertainty around AI narrative and expecting the stock to remain rangebound. D.A. Davidson upgrades MDB to Buy based on positive field conversations at MongoDB.local; UBS notes customer feedback shows durable spend but no material AI-driven inflection yet.

bullets.title: AAPL: Morgan Stanley cuts PT to $355 (from $360); 35x valuation a concern despite strong roadmap
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley maintains Overweight on AAPL but trims PT to $355, flagging peak valuation at 35x P/E as a constraint. Forecasts ~$10 EPS FY27 and ~$11 FY28 (0-3% above Street); iPhone unit growth next 2+ years seen as strongest since FY15. Dec quarter setup viewed as mixed. Hedgeye signals AAPL bullish range 328-345.

bullets.title: TSM: JPM raises PT to NT$3,300; leading-edge supply tight through 2028, capex to $100B
bullets.body: JPM raises TSMC PT to NT$3,300 on strong 3Q26 results (revenue at guidance high-end ~$45.8B, GM 66.8%) and healthy 4Q26 guidance (+11% QoQ, N3-capacity limited). FY27/28 EPS raised 5%/6%; 2027/28 capex projected at $86B/$100B on faster N3/N2 ramp. A14 production may pull forward with revenue contribution in 2H28. AI wafer supply tight extending into 2028.

bullets.title: NBIS: Acquires Inferize to strengthen Token Factory inference platform
bullets.body: Nebius acquired Inferize, an inference optimization company, to enhance its Token Factory managed inference platform. Inferize's technology shortens time to launch and scale large AI models; joins prior acquisitions Eigen AI and Clarifai. Terms undisclosed. NBIS +1.4% pre-mkt.

bullets.title: NVDA: Bubble sentiment flag from Weniger; Hedgeye bullish range 219-233
bullets.body: Macro commentator Jeff Weniger flagged Nvidia's "widespread popularity" as a potential sign of bubble-like sentiment, while noting rising power demand from data centers supports energy allocation. Hedgeye maintains NVDA in bullish trade range 219-233. Separately, UBS notes NVDA's de-speccing of Rubin Ultra spreads limited HBM supply, creating latent demand materializing in the Feynman generation (mid-late 2028).

bullets.title: NFLX: Co-CEO Sarandos admits growth slower than desired; Hedgeye bearish range 67-72
bullets.body: Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos stated the company is "not growing as fast as I want" and is working to accelerate growth through live content expansion. Hedgeye maintains NFLX in bearish trade range 67-72. JPM notes the user content library is viewed as insufficient.

bullets.title: RDDT: Shutting down RSS feeds Nov 13, public API March 2027 to combat AI scraping; DAU risk
bullets.body: Reddit is shutting down RSS feeds on November 13 and the public API on March 2027 to combat AI scraping. JPM notes this risks further US DAU decline despite logged-in user growth.

bullets.title: AI data center regulatory map shrinking; benefits permitted-capacity holders like CRWV
bullets.body: A Midterms analysis notes U.S. AI data center demand estimated at 107 GW through 2030 but only ~70 GW has confirmed offtake and defined locations. AI-friendly states drop from 27 to ~15 post-midterms; Texas (47% of announced capacity) faces ERCOT queue review impacting 70-80% of state projects in 2027-28. Over 800 local moratoria since June 2025; 16% of US counties now have regulatory restrictions. Compute supply shortage likely to worsen, benefiting companies with approved/permitted capacity.

bullets.title: OpenAI competitive threat to MSFT/GOOGL intensifies with Dots agents and GPT-6.1 Sol
bullets.body: OpenAI launched Dots agents (24/7 persistent context across 4,000+ apps) expanding into territory served by Microsoft and Google. GPT-6.1 Sol matches frontier Astra performance at one-fifth the cost with cached input pricing 95% below standard. OpenAI's 1.2B weekly users and ChatGPT sign-in as distribution channel for third-party developers creates a platform competitive with Microsoft's and Google's ecosystems.
